So I finally wrapped up Tomb Raider, having picked it up in the Winter Sale. I missed it the first time round, and having enjoyed the Uncharted series on PS3, I thought it was worth nabbing it at the low cost, and I made it even lower by selling most of the Steam trading cards I had lying around, which I had been meaning to getting around to doing anyway.

I played the PC version with the PCS+ R9 290, having the graphics gunned up to the nines. Being a card from 2013 itself (and actually released around 6 months after the game) my card was running at some pretty high temps fairly quickly (around the 70-80 degree mark), but this is normal for the 290 given it's standard operating temperature. That said, the graphics menu was always within easy reach if I needed to turn them down, and I also had good airflow. Never hurts to test the boundaries, though, and the results were fairly beautiful. There were no tearing, stuttering, or any similar issues, etc, and I was happy with the performance. I didn't do the benchmark test or test the FPS, but it would've been easily at least 60, if not higher.

Story-wise, however, I felt it almost crumbled a bit. It made sense in a, sort of, storyboard fashion. Y'know, event leads to event, which leads to event, which leads to event etc. But the reboot is re-establishing the already established lore of her backstory. To be quite honest, I wasn't sure what the original backstory was (I've slept since the originals), but from what the wiki page suggests, there wasn't really much of a need to re-write her backstory? Anyway. Y'know, console crowds and younger players. I'm not too fussed about the backstory thing, but I just felt it was the wrong move? Hmmm.

The actual story though, is fairly cliché, honestly. There's some foreshadowing going on, and it's not too hard to guess the plot by the way things go. The pacing is also pretty quick, which helps to keep things moving along, and back into the swing of things for the next time you play - if like me, you play over multiple days - but the actual amount of story content is fairly limited, and the game can be blitzed in a few hours if you know what you're doing. My Steam time says 8 hours, and whilst I wouldn't say it felt 'short' (I mean, the Uncharted games weren't exactly 20-hour escapades either), I guess I felt a little reeled in too soon. There were a couple more mechanics I'd have liked to see fleshed out, and I feel that the plot wouldn't feel so short. For example, early into the game, you're tasked with hunting an animal. You only perform this task once, as you never need to do it again. Some sort of prompt from Lara - 'Man, I could use a bite to eat', or some effect like swayed aiming and slower movement, would indicate I need to go hunt again.

I understand it would be kinda hard to implement this, or any similar mechanics, without making it an open world game with a shit ton of back-tracking, but the ability to fast travel between camps was available. I'm not sure what the inclusion was for except to offer an easy way to jump around and pick up collectibles and the like, even though the reward it offers, if any, is most likely negligible. Had a little more thought gone this way, y'know, and a little less linearity, I think it could've been something a little more special. The actual plot, though, was fairly concise and cohesive, if a little retarded, and although offering very limited freedom in how to approach enemies, I paid the entry fee and enjoyed what I saw. The whole 'Bildungsroman' style of Lara overpowering the odds was there, with the whole 'strong independent female lead' vibe throughout. I'm not saying I didn't like it, but the pep talks throughout just really slapped me across the face with this. Uncharted has Nathan Drake - a cocky adventurer who causes trouble for the sake of it, but all around likeable good guy because "they must be the bad guys because they shot first". Tomb Raider, however, goes for a very hardcore vibe and tries to hit you with the feels, which I don't feel works as well in a genre built for setpieces. And there's plenty of them within Tomb Raider.

Overall, though, I have to say I quite enjoyed it. I'm more of a single player guy, so I very much appreciate a well crafted story with twists and turns in the narrative to keep you on edge. However, I also can enjoy nabbing a game on the cheap, kicking back on an off day, and just playing for shits and giggles. Tomb Raider doesn't have much going for it now, given that the whole 'reboot' vibe has more than worn off (and a re-release is out for the PS4/One with a new lick of paint), but I enjoyed what I saw. If the price is right, I'd pick it up.

I'd actually say I'm interested in the recently released sequel, Rise of the Tomb Raider, to continue the reboot's story, but that entry fee is looking pretty high.

6/10: Some pretty graphics, and average gameplay is accompanied by a fairly weak and short story with some linear gameplay. However, to kick back on an afternoon and play through a dozen different setpieces was nice, especially considering what I personally paid. Time well spent.
